newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 3.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 3.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:

** The Indian government said on Thursday that an exemption from long-term capital gains tax which was announced on Wednesday applies to shares issued by publicly-traded companies involved in infrastructure work.
On Wednesday, the government released an order allowing
investment in shares issued by public companies to be exempt from long-term capital gains tax. The statement did not specify which public companies were covered by the order.
Krishna Saini, deputy secretary of the tax policy
division in the Finance Ministry, told Reuters that public limited companies whose shares are widely traded are eligible to be covered.

** The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) expects to start a share depository by April this year, its chief said. "India Securities Depository Ltd is expected to start working by April 1997," BSE president Madan Gopal Damani said at a news conference.
The depository immobilises share certificates, eliminates
cumbersome physical transfer of shares whenever these are bought or sold and ushers in paperless trading.
India's first share depository was launched in November
by BSE rival, the National Stock Exchange which operates in 53 centres across the country.

** Reliance Industries is considering a combination of American Depository Receipts, Yankee bonds, external commercial borrowings, term loans and internal accruals to finance its 43 billion rupee paraxylene project to be set up in the western state of Gujarat, the Business Standard says.

** The country's top banking and financial institutionas have entered the market in the past three days to raise more than 27 billion rupees through issue of bonds to retail and bulk investors, the Economic Times reports.
** The Indian rupee opened steady at 35.92/94 per dollar on Friday and is seen range-bound, dealers said.
MARKETS:
** Stocks across Indian bourses retreated on Thursday on profit-booking after soaring 5.7 percent on Wednesday.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index
fell 35.32 points, or 1.08 percent, to end at 3,225.62.
The 50-stock index of the National Stock Exchange (NSE)
index lost 12.50 points, or 1.33 percent, to 927.05.
The Delhi index dropped 7.40 points, or 1.04
percent, to 704.85.
